text:
Ben C.: Heads up — LumaHealth POC asking for a Dedicated commit carveout in EMEA. They want 4x A100 baseline with a 2-week test window that can burst up to ~40 A100-equivalent. Sales asked if we can offer a flat burst rate cap (so they don't face per-minute spikes). Need deal-desk & finance signoff.

Alexa M.: do we have precedent for flat burst caps on short-term POCs? I recall a similar ask but not for that scale.

Carmen R.: we did a capped burst for Atlas last year but they committed >12 months. Short POCs are riskier. What's the proposed pricing math?

Ben C.: proposal from sales_ops below (sketch):
```
Commit: 4x A100 reserved (monthly sku)
Baseline capacity: 4 GPUs (always available)
POC burst window: 14 days (can spike to 40 A100-equivalent pooled)
Proposed commercial: 15% commit discount on baseline + capped burst rate at $6.50/hr per A100-equivalent during window (flat), with a hard cap of $10k total burst charges for the 14d window.
Operational ask: allow autoscale to 40 in EMEA for that window and guarantee fallback to smaller model variants if capacity constrained.
```

Priya (sales_ops): LumaHealth wants a single predictable line item for the customer — they cannot accept metered per-minute burst billing in their procurement. They've pushed legal to require a cap.

Tom E. (eng-runtime): from infra side we can gate the burst with quota + autoscale policy. Two things to flag: 1) we need pre-reserved capacity or else the burst will rely on best-effort spot-style capacity which violates the customer's ask; 2) supporting a hard-dollar cap means we must track and enforce usage at the platform level to avoid cost leakage.

Ivy (finance): flat burst cap is doable but we need to model tail risk. If they actually hit 40 GPUs for the full 14 days, the marginal cost to us could exceed the capped revenue. Need an expected-utilization assumption or a refundable deposit. Suggest either: refundable overage deposit of $X or reduce burst cap to 20 GPUs.

Carmen R.: two follow-ups — (a) can we offer a middle-ground: guaranteed baseline 4 GPUs + pre-booked burst pool of 8 GPUs reserved for the window, and best-effort beyond that but with a cap? (b) legal will want explicit fallback behavior documented (i.e., if burst cannot be satisfied we downgrade to quantized model with degraded latency).

Ben C.: I can push both options to LumaHealth. Sales prefers the $10k flat cap route to close contract this week. If we go that route, what ops/instrumentation work do we need and how long?

Tom E. (eng-runtime): instrumentation: billing meter + quota enforcement + a circuit that stops serving burst requests once cap is reached. Implementation estimate: 5 business days to add a per-deal cap enforcement and dashboard, assuming eng-sre prioritizes it. If we require reserved GPUs for the burst pool, provisioning lead time is 7–10 days.

Priya (sales_ops): timeline matters — POC kickoff targeted next Monday. If we can't provision reserved burst capacity in time, customer will push start by 2 weeks. They prefer to start.

Ivy (finance): if timeline short, insist on refundable deposit to cover worst-case. We can reconcile afterward and refund unused portion. That protects Redwood.

Carmen R.: deal-desk checklist before approval:
- Confirm exact GPU SKUs (A100S vs older A100)
- Finalize duration and hard cap amount in USD
- Signed fallback SLA language (through legal)
- Define rollback plan if burst unavailable
- Internal ops tickets for quota/provisioning + billing enforcement

Ben C.: ok I'll push two options to customer: (1) baseline 4x reserved + prebooked 8x burst reserved + best-effort beyond with cap; (2) baseline 4x reserved + full 40-equivalent best-effort burst with $10k capped charge + refundable deposit.

Alexa M.: tagging @Ivy @Tom E. please confirm if finance + runtime can sign off on option 2 with deposit and 5-day delivery for instrumentation. If yes, sales can close next week.

Tom E. (eng-runtime): can sign off on the 5-day instrumentation timeline if eng-sre deprioritization risk is accepted by sales/product. Can't commit to reserved capacity provisioning in 5 days.

Ivy (finance): okay to approve option 2 with a refundable deposit equal to the modeled worst-case incremental cost for 14d at 40 GPUs. I'll compute the number and post it in channel by EOD.

deploy-bot: Incident check: no ongoing infra incidents in EMEA; capacity pool available: medium.

Priya (sales_ops): thanks everyone — Ben, please share the two-option email to LumaHealth and include the deposit amount once Ivy posts it. I'll prepare the draft commercial term sheet.

Ben C.: will do. posting draft email in #sales-drafts and looping in legal.

Alexa M.: thanks team — once Ivy posts numbers and legal signs the fallback SLA we can route to the deal desk for final signoff. :thumbsup:
